searchText: Politicking this is more than mildly worrisome to me, but I don't want to get into that meta-issue. My main point is that saving a byte or so in the size of contracts is truly irrelevant. Issues involving SELFDESTRUCT, syncing and such probably are, but I'd need more time and long-form analysis to get clear on them. I'm glad to see the authors of the relevant EIPs here, and trust them to get it right in the end. <@!273808422753796097> > Isn't it standard to pretend all contracts come attached with an infinite right tail of zero bytes? Yes, the Yellow Paper is clear on that.
